reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent (Opus 4.8), separate context — verify pass + scoped fix re-review

records.finding: The reconciler recorded a SUCCESS at pi.AmountReceived (captured), but the webhook telemetry path this ledger is reconciled against records a succeeded payment_intent at pi.Amount (intended). On a partial capture the two sides measure different money for the same event, producing a false coverage shortfall — the opposite of the 'reconciles to 100%' goal.
records.evidence: classify returned pi.AmountReceived for success while stripe.go eventMap uses amtAmount (object.Amount) for EventTypePaymentIntentSucceeded; only success diverged (failed/deferred already used Amount).
records.reason: classify now returns (biz.Result, bool) and Reconcile sums pi.Amount for EVERY outcome, matching the webhook basis so both sides measure the same money and a partial capture reconciles to 100%. The doc states the basis and the (tracked) partial-capture-shortfall tradeoff. Verified: AmountReceived no longer appears in production code.

records.finding: TestReconcileAggregatesAndReconciles100 was self-referential: it summed the reconciler's OWN output rows and compared to fixture totals computed on the same basis the reconciler used, so it could not detect the amount-basis divergence — its '100%' was a tautology.
records.evidence: Old test asserted USD total against 14000 (10000+AmountReceived 4000), the reconciler's own basis, never an independent telemetry-basis sum.
records.reason: Rewrote the assertion as a hand-derived expected table on the intended-amount (telemetry) basis, with pi_2 a partial capture (amount 5000, received 4000) counted at 5000 -> checkout USD success 15000. A revert to AmountReceived yields 14000 and fails the test, making it a real regression guard; each row is Validate-checked and the row count asserted.

records.finding: classify() was tested only indirectly via Reconcile; the reviewer flagged the default branch and requires_confirmation/requires_action as untested.
records.evidence: Reviewer claimed the default branch had no fixture.
records.reason: The as-stated claim was REFUTED by the cross-examiner: the default branch was already exercised via pi_8 (requires_capture -> skip, asserted in Skipped==2). The genuine partial gap (requires_confirmation/requires_action, both branches) was nonetheless closed by adding TestClassify, a direct table over every classify branch including default and an unknown/future status.

records.finding: The already-merged webhook 'object' struct has no amount_received field, so a succeeded PaymentIntent is always recorded at the intended amount; on a partial capture the telemetry side overstates realized value versus money actually captured. This is the telemetry-side root of the basis question.
records.evidence: stripe.go object struct (json fields amount/amount_paid/amount_due, no amount_received); eventMap succeeded -> amtAmount.
records.reason: Out of scope for this PR: it touches merged/frozen webhook code and the canonical basis (intended vs captured) is an ADR decision, not a silent change. The reconciler was deliberately aligned to the SAME (intended) basis so coverage measures drift, not capture policy. Parked as bead workspace-tmw.6.4, which requires an ADR and, if amount_received is chosen, a coordinated change to BOTH paths.

records.finding: After the basis fix, the pi test-helper comment ('received ... used for success') was stale, since AmountReceived is no longer read by the reconciler.
records.evidence: Helper comment described a use that the fix removed.
